name: Asceticism
overview: Scripture presents asceticism as a practice with both commendable and cautionary aspects. John the Baptist exemplifies ascetic living by abstaining from food and drink, yet he faced accusations of being demon-possessed, while Jesus, who engaged in ordinary eating and drinking, was criticized as a glutton and drunkard, highlighting the misunderstanding surrounding such lifestyles (Matthew 11:18-19; Luke 7:33-34). Additionally, Jesus acknowledges those who choose celibacy for the kingdom of heaven, indicating a voluntary, kingdom-focused ascetic commitment (Matthew 19:12). However, Paul warns believers against submitting to worldly ordinances, implying that extreme ascetic practices rooted in legalism are not fitting for those dead to the world in Christ (Colossians 2:20). Thus, Scripture recognizes asceticism when motivated by sincere devotion but rebukes its extreme or legalistic applications.
